strongest_objection: The map's discovery is that the trade designs exits one level above the contract, and the two edges that carry that passage are wrong in their specifics. Runoff → Sell the seat says a runoff book sold to a legacy acquirer is 'a sale of the seat to a stranger at a discount', but a book of open liabilities is a seat whose value is below zero: the leaver pays the stranger to sit in it, and the substitute is accepted not by the stayers but by a regulator or court on the policyholders' behalf, so the label has the money running the wrong way and omits the consent that makes it a seat sale at all. Sell the seat → Drag and tag says the trade-level market exists where entry terms pre-granted consent 'as tag rights and free assignability do', but a tag right does not let anyone sell a seat; it lets the minority join the majority's sale of the house. The clauses that pre-grant a seat sale are free assignability, consent not to be unreasonably withheld, and the right of first refusal, and drag and tag are the same pre-grant applied to the whole house. Both edges are repairable without touching the items and the passage survives the repair, which is why this is admit-with-repairs rather than return. A third fault is bookkeeping: the breath-one ledger says the insurance-funded buy-sell was merged into the Shotgun → Veil edge 'as the antecedent of the fork', and the recorded label does not mention it, so the merge lost what it claimed to keep. Beyond these I tried to break the item type with an earn-out and a right of first refusal, and the closest pair I could find with a queue and a chair, and the type held; the items are mechanisms, the strange members are kept strange, and the residue rejections are real.

items.item: Shotgun at the table: at deadlock either partner names a single price and the other must choose to buy or sell at it, so the namer prices honestly because they do not yet know which side of the trade they will stand on, as in the buy-sell clauses of two-person contracting firms; conserved is the business whole under one owner and a price nobody argued, the cost falls on the partner who cannot fund the buy, who sells at whatever the richer one names, and the next entrant learns to compare purses before signing; not a formula, since the price is discovered by the leaving itself, and it cannot be improvised because nobody names a price blind once they know they are the buyer.
items.why: The discriminator's reason it cannot be improvised is muddled: in a shotgun the namer never knows which side they will stand on, so 'nobody names a price blind once they know they are the buyer' describes a game that does not exist. The real reason is the purse: once purses are known, the poorer partner refuses a game whose only move for them is to sell. The mechanism sentence is right; only the last clause needed the correct mechanism.
items.repair: Shotgun at the table: at deadlock either partner names a single price and the other must choose to buy or sell at it, so the namer prices honestly because they do not yet know which side of the trade they will stand on, as in the buy-sell clauses of two-person contracting firms; conserved is the business whole under one owner and a price nobody argued, the cost falls on the partner who cannot fund the buy, who sells at whatever the richer one names, and the next entrant learns to compare purses before signing; not a formula, since the price is discovered by the leaving itself, and it cannot be improvised because the partner with the smaller purse, once purses are known, refuses a game whose only move for them is to sell.

items.item: Fade by formula: the partner who stops answering capital calls is not expelled but diluted on a schedule fixed at entry, as a venture syndicate's pay-to-play terms convert a non-participant's preferred shares to common at each round they sit out; conserved is the venture and the room, since nobody is thrown out and nobody leaves, the cost falls on the fader in slices with no single day to contest, and the next entrant learns that exit here is a slope, not a step; not a vesting cliff, which makes leaving a date around which the roster clusters at month thirteen, and not expulsion, since the fader may stop fading at any call.
items.why: The item says 'nobody leaves', which is exactly what the map's second boundary claim excludes (departures in which the party never really leaves), and the declared type requires that a party leave something. The fader does leave something nameable: the syndicate's calls and its preference. Saying so keeps the item inside its own type.
items.repair: Fade by formula: the partner who stops answering capital calls is not expelled but diluted on a schedule fixed at entry, as a venture syndicate's pay-to-play terms convert a non-participant's preferred shares to common at each round they sit out; conserved is the venture and the room, since nobody is thrown out and what the fader leaves is the syndicate's calls and its preference while their common stays on the cap table, the cost falls on the fader in slices with no single day to contest, and the next entrant learns that exit here is a slope, not a step; not a vesting cliff, which makes leaving a date around which the roster clusters at month thirteen, and not expulsion, since the fader may stop fading at any call.

items.item: Queue at the door: exits are paced so that leaving does not force the sale that would hurt those who stay, as a fund redeems quarterly on ninety days' notice with a gate at a tenth of assets, and an executive's notice period holds the seat until the search is done; conserved is the stayers' value, the cost falls on the leaver in time, and the next entrant reads the queue's length as the printed illiquidity of what they are buying into; time, not money, and a gate written into the documents kept in 2008 the trust that a gate improvised that year destroyed.
items.why: Two faults. The second illustrative case, a notice period that 'holds the seat until the search is done', is the mechanism of Chair filled before it's empty (a conditional date), not a queue (a fixed duration); the queue's own case leaked into its neighbor. And 'a gate written into the documents kept in 2008 the trust that a gate improvised that year destroyed' asserts an illustrative reading as documented history; some funds with document gates were sued and some ad hoc suspensions were forgiven, so it must be stated as the authored reading it is.
items.repair: Queue at the door: exits are paced so that leaving does not force the sale that would hurt those who stay, as a fund redeems quarterly on ninety days' notice with a gate at a tenth of assets, and an executive's notice period holds the seat for a fixed term whether or not a successor has been found; conserved is the stayers' value, the cost falls on the leaver in time, and the next entrant reads the queue's length as the printed illiquidity of what they are buying into; time, not money, and a gate the leaver signed at entry is read as the terms while a gate imposed by amendment on the day is read as a default, offered as the reading of why some 2008 gates kept their investors and others lost them.

items.item: Swing price: the leaver's exit price is adjusted by the trading cost their leaving imposes on the stayers, so a redemption on a bad day is paid out at a value reduced by exactly what it cost the fund to raise the cash; conserved is the stayers' value to the cent, the cost falls on the leaver in the amount of their own haste, and the next entrant learns that an exit has a price and it is printed on the confirm; money, not time, so a queue defers the harm while a swing charges it, and unlike an exit fee the amount is not fixed but measured on the day.
items.why: 'Reduced by exactly what it cost the fund' and 'to the cent' promote a mechanism to a precision it does not have: a swing factor is an estimate of dealing costs set in advance, and partial swing pricing applies only when net flows cross a threshold. The mechanism is unchanged; the modality is corrected.
items.repair: Swing price: the leaver's exit price is adjusted by the trading cost their leaving imposes on the stayers, so a redemption on a bad day is paid out at a value reduced by an estimate of what it cost the fund to raise the cash, applied once net outflows cross a threshold; conserved is the stayers' value, as nearly as the estimate is right, the cost falls on the leaver in the amount of their own haste, and the next entrant learns that an exit has a price and it is printed on the confirm; money, not time, so a queue defers the harm while a swing charges it, and unlike an exit fee the amount is not fixed but measured on the day.

items.item: House kept on the children's clock: the divorcing spouse who leaves has their share of the house frozen in it until the youngest child is eighteen, the Mesher order of English family courts; conserved is a third party's use of the very thing the parties are dividing, the cost falls on the leaver in years of illiquidity, and the next entrant learns that some exits run on a non-party's clock; not a deferred sale by agreement, since a court imposes it on parties who could not agree, and the beneficiary is neither of them.
items.why: The discriminator rests on imposition ('since a court imposes it on parties who could not agree'), but Mesher orders are routinely made by consent. What earns the item its stage is not that a court forced it but that the clock belongs to a non-party even when the parties agree; the repair moves the discriminator onto that.
items.repair: House kept on the children's clock: the divorcing spouse who leaves has their share of the house frozen in it until the youngest child is eighteen, the Mesher order of English family courts; conserved is a third party's use of the very thing the parties are dividing, the cost falls on the leaver in years of illiquidity, and the next entrant learns that some exits run on a non-party's clock; not a deferred sale by agreement, since a court can impose it on parties who could not agree and the clock belongs to neither of them even when they consent to it.

items.item: Chair filled before it's empty: the exit is dated by the successor's existence rather than the leaver's readiness, as a chief executive announces departure only in the sentence that names who follows; conserved is continuity of command with no vacancy for factions to fill, the cost falls on the leaver, who serves past their wish, and on the successor, who is known before they hold power, and the next entrant learns whether a bench existed; not a notice period, which is a duration, but a conditional date, and it can be improvised by any leaver willing to wait.
items.why: Tested as the right neighbor below against Queue at the door; it separates on the day the search fails, and the repair to Queue removes the one case that blurred them.

items.item: Leave the comb: the leaver takes only what walks, people and know-how, and forfeits every fixed asset to the stayers, as a swarm leaves with the old queen and half the workers and abandons comb, brood, stores, and a capped queen cell; conserved is the fixed capital, whole under the stayers, the cost falls on the leaver, who rebuilds from nothing fixed, and on the stayers, who lose half their hands, and the next entrant learns that what walked was never the firm's; an analogy from the hive, not a claim about bees, and not a fork, since nothing is copied, nor a buyout, since nothing is paid; the timing, leaving when the cell is capped rather than when the new queen emerges, is offered as speculation about firms.
items.why: The item is the seriation's endpoint and the map's wild opening, and it carries no case from any trade, only the hive; the brief admits a remote domain when it sharpens a mechanism drawn from a trade, not in place of one. The lift-out, a desk or team that walks from a bank with its know-how and whichever clients follow and leaves the book, the desks, and the name, is the plain business instance and makes 'what walked was never the firm's' checkable. The hive, its marking as analogy, and the timing speculation are preserved untouched.
items.repair: Leave the comb: the leaver takes only what walks, people and know-how, and forfeits every fixed asset to the stayers, as a trading desk lifted out of a bank walks with its know-how and whichever clients follow and leaves the book, the desks, and the name, and as a swarm leaves with the old queen and half the workers and abandons comb, brood, stores, and a capped queen cell; conserved is the fixed capital, whole under the stayers, the cost falls on the leaver, who rebuilds from nothing fixed, and on the stayers, who lose half their hands, and the next entrant learns that what walked was never the firm's; the hive is an analogy, not a claim about bees, and this is not a fork, since nothing is copied, nor a buyout, since nothing is paid; the timing, leaving when the cell is capped rather than when the new queen emerges, is offered as speculation about firms.

neighbor_test.left: Queue at the door: exits are paced so that leaving does not force the sale that would hurt those who stay, as a fund redeems quarterly on ninety days' notice with a gate at a tenth of assets, and an executive's notice period holds the seat until the search is done; conserved is the stayers' value, the cost falls on the leaver in time, and the next entrant reads the queue's length as the printed illiquidity of what they are buying into; time, not money, and a gate written into the documents kept in 2008 the trust that a gate improvised that year destroyed.
neighbor_test.right: Chair filled before it's empty: the exit is dated by the successor's existence rather than the leaver's readiness, as a chief executive announces departure only in the sentence that names who follows; conserved is continuity of command with no vacancy for factions to fill, the cost falls on the leaver, who serves past their wish, and on the successor, who is known before they hold power, and the next entrant learns whether a bench existed; not a notice period, which is a duration, but a conditional date, and it can be improvised by any leaver willing to wait.
neighbor_test.separating_case: A chief financial officer resigns. Under the queue, the contract fixes ninety days, and on the ninety-first the seat is empty whether or not a replacement has signed, so the board searches against a date the leaver set and the cost of a slow search falls on the stayers. Under the chair, the letter reads 'effective on my successor's start date', a failed search keeps the leaver in the seat for a year, and the leaver has no date at all, so the cost of a slow search falls on the leaver and the board holds the clock. They are told apart on the day the search fails: the queue empties the seat and the chair does not. The pair did not collapse, but the Queue item's own second case, a notice period that 'holds the seat until the search is done', is the chair's mechanism wearing the queue's name, which is why Queue is repaired rather than merged.

boundary_case: An earn-out: the seller leaves and is paid over three years from the business's own results. It is tempting because it is fixed at the door between known parties and something survives (the deal, across a valuation gap). It is out: what it conserves is the closability of a price, not anything the default exit would have destroyed; the seller leaves on the same day either way, and the device belongs to impasse-inventions as a synthetic bargaining chip. Against it I tested a right of first refusal, and that one is in: fixed at entry behind the veil, it lets a partner leave to a stranger while conserving the stayers' choice of who sits in the seat, the cost falls on the leaver in the bids a matchable offer chills, and the next entrant learns their seat's market has a matcher in it. The type admits it and the list lacks it, which is the second reason the Sell the seat → Drag and tag edge names the wrong clause: the pre-grant that makes a seat market is the assignability or first-refusal clause, not the tag.

seriation.note: The axis has real endpoints (terms fixed at entry behind a veil; nothing fixed at all) and the claimed adjacency Sell the seat → Reinsurance to close does teach: the buyer of the exit shifts from a stranger to the stayers and the price from a discount to a premium, and when the stayers cannot price it nobody leaves. Two weaknesses to record. The third stage, terms fixed by a third party at the door, has one member, and it is from family law; the business members of that stage exist and are missing, the judicial fair-value buyout ordered in a shareholder-oppression suit in place of dissolution, and the antitrust divestiture to a buyer the agency approves under a hold-separate order, both of which conserve a going concern the default exit would have liquidated. And Runoff's placement among exits improvised at the door is arguable, since its terms are the policies' own promises, each fixed at that customer's entry; only the decision to write nothing new is improvised. Neither breaks the itinerary.

edges.why: The breath-one ledger merged the insurance-funded buy-sell ('Premium paid for the funeral') into this edge and says it was 'kept as the antecedent of the fork edge', but the recorded label never mentions it, so the merge lost what it claimed to keep. Restoring it also makes the fork three-pronged in the way an operator actually meets it: discover the price, fund the buy in advance, or fix a formula.
edges.repair_label: If the two purses are unequal, the shotgun degrades into a forced sale by the poorer partner at whatever price the richer one names, and the pair must either fund the buy in advance, as life insurance on each partner funds a buy-sell at death, or fall back to a formula; the fork at entry is discovery against fundability, and which branch is safe is decided by the partners' bank balances, not by the business.

edges.to_handle: Sell the seat, not the house
edges.why: The label has the money running the wrong way and omits the consent that makes it a seat sale. A runoff book sold to a legacy acquirer is not a seat sold to a stranger at a discount; the seat is all promise and its value is below zero, so the leaver pays the stranger to sit in it. And the substitute is accepted not by the stayers but by a regulator or court on the policyholders' behalf, which is the element that connects it to Sell the seat's 'a substitute the stayers accept'. The passage between levels survives once the label says this.
edges.repair_label: If enough insurers are running off books at once, a buyer of tails appears, and the leaver's decade of holding becomes a transfer of the seat to a stranger whom a regulator or court accepts on the policyholders' behalf, the leaver paying the stranger to sit in it, since a seat that is all promise sells at a price below zero; the deal's improvised exit becomes the trade's designed one, so the line between designed and improvised is drawn not by the contract but by how old the trade is.

edges.from_handle: Sell the seat, not the house
edges.why: A tag right does not pre-grant consent to sell a seat; it lets the minority join the majority's sale of the whole house. The clauses that make a seat market are free assignability, consent not to be unreasonably withheld, and the right of first refusal (which converts the stayers' veto into a match). The dependency the author wants is real, so the repair keeps the edge and names the right clause, and says what drag and tag actually are in this light: the same pre-grant applied to the whole house.
edges.repair_label: If the seat can be sold only with the stayers' consent, a market for seats exists only where the entry papers pre-granted it, by free assignability, by consent not to be unreasonably withheld, or by a right of first refusal that lets the stayers match rather than veto; drag and tag are the same pre-grant applied to the whole house, since the majority's buyer must take or may take the minority's seat too, and where the papers say nothing every seat sale is a renegotiation with the stayers holding the pen.

edges.why: The incompatibility is real inside a venture that ends on schedule, but 'the trade attaches its names to persons instead, as film credits do' ignores the banner: a per-picture company sunsets while the production banner one level up keeps its name across pictures. The name is not lost to the trade; it moves up a level. Saying so sharpens rather than softens the incompatibility.
edges.repair_label: If the charter sunsets, no name outlives the venture, so no name can stay on its door; the trade attaches its names to persons or to a banner one level up, as film credits and production banners do, and the exit that keeps the name is impossible inside a venture that ends on schedule, which is why the two are never found in the same house.

modality_problems: Queue at the door asserts as history that document gates kept trust in 2008 while improvised gates destroyed it; repaired to an authored reading.
Swing price says the leaver is charged 'exactly' the cost and the stayers are protected 'to the cent'; swing factors are pre-set estimates applied above a flow threshold; repaired.
Shotgun at the table's discriminator gives a mechanism for non-improvisability that describes no real game (the namer never knows their side); repaired to the purse.
House kept on the children's clock discriminates on court imposition, but Mesher orders are commonly consent orders; repaired onto the non-party clock.

Reinsurance to close says the closed year's members 'walk free of it forever'; RITC is a contract of reinsurance, not a novation, so in law the members remain liable if the reinsuring year fails, a residue the Central Fund makes practically moot. Left as written under the map's stated simplification, but recorded here so the sentence is not read as the legal position.
The Everyone leaves at once → Name stays on the door label treats film names as attaching to persons only; production banners carry names across sunsetting ventures; repaired.
The Chair filled before it's empty → Leave the comb label and Leave the comb's last clause are speculation and are marked as such in the item, the edge, the mode, and the boundary claims; no problem.
duplication: none. Adjacencies the map should name that it does not: impasse-inventions' 'The sunset: a dated release from obligations that makes a limited term negotiable' is the same device as Everyone leaves at once seen as a bargaining chip rather than as the abolition of leaving; deal-flow-attractors' 'Written first look' (the right of first refusal) is the clause the seat-sale dependency edge should name; cooperation-integrity-hinges' 'Liability horizon' asks what backs a harm after the project ends, and Runoff and Reinsurance to close answer who holds the tail and who pays for it. No item restates any of them.
best_unresolved_seed: The Leave the comb → Dividing the curtain edge points at a stage it does not contain: a trade custom that blesses what walks without lending a name. The Protocol for Broker Recruiting is that stage in a real trade: the wirehouses agreed in 2004 not to sue departing brokers who take only client names and leave everything else, and the custom is testable because the firms that withdrew from it in 2017 resumed suing their swarms. Sitting between the swarm and the curtain, it would let the passage edge be read against documents rather than a hive, and it asks the operator's question directly: what does a trade get from blessing its swarms that it loses by suing them?
independent_review_line: Fable critic: admitted after repairing the two edges that carried the deal-to-trade passage (a runoff book is a seat sold below zero, and tag rights do not pre-grant a seat sale), restoring the insurance-funded buy-sell the ledger said it kept in the fork edge, and repairing five items for modality, for a case that leaked from the queue into the chair, and for a trade instance missing from the swarm.
